UNICRAZE: The Ground-Up Brand 
Playbook  
Division: MM&C (Marketing, Media & Communications) 
Vibe: Build in Public. Start Sma l. Scale Smart. 
Listen, marketing isn’t a 30-day magic trick. You can’t just run a campaign for one month and 
expect a cult folowing. We are building a brand from scratch, figuring out our voice, and 
bringing people along for the ride. We don’t need a massive, noisy launch. We need a subtle 
entry, high-quality aesthetics, and a "building in public" narrative. 
Here is exactly how we are going to execute this over the next 3-6 months. (DEPENDING ON 
THE NEXT MOVES AND PRODUCT) 
1. The Bare Minimum (What we need from the 
Founders) 
We don't need a 50-page thesis or endless resources right now. We just need the keys to the 
car so we can start driving. 
● The "Why" & The Story: Just a quick brain-dump from you guys. Why did you start this? 
What's the one problem that makes you angry enough to build Unicraze? (We wil use this 
for our storyte ling). 
● Basic Assets & Access: Current logos (even if they are drafts), brand colors you like, and 
admin access to whatever social pages or domains we currently own. 
● A Tiny Tool Budget: Just the absolute basics to pay for a couple of SaaS tools (listed 
below) so we can automate our lives and focus on creating, not doing manual data entry. 
2. The Masterplan (What we will do for Unicraze) 
We are treating Unicraze like a creator-led brand. People connect with people and processes, 
not just websites. 
Phase 1: The Vibe Check & Foundation (Month 1) 
We aren't launching yet. We are building the engine. 
● The Mood Board: We wil build a visual mood board. Are we sleek and techy? Are we edgy 
and student-focused? We wil lock down the exact visual vibe. 
● Template Factory: Designing plug-and-play templates for Instagram, LinkedIn, and 
Twitter. When we need to post an update, an event, or a meme, we shouldn't be designing 
from scratch. 
● "Building in Public" Content: We start documenting the journey. "Hey, we are building 
Unicraze for students. Here’s what the website looks like today. Here is what we messed 
up." People love raw, behind-the-scenes content. 
Phase 2: The Subtle Soft Launch (Month 2) 
No big fireworks. Just sliding into the DMs of the internet. 
● The 100 True Fans Strategy: We quietly invite a smal, curated group of students and club 
heads to the platform. We treat them like VIPs. (SOCH NA HOGA FOR THIS) 
● Feedback Loop: We use this month to gather testimonials, fix broken links, and see how 
users actua ly use the site. 
● Content Shift: Our social media shifts from "we are building this" to "look at what these 
early users are doing with this." (THIS FS) 
Phase 3: The Distribution Engine (Month 3) 
Now that the foundation is set and the brand looks premium, we turn up the volume. 
● Automated Content Pipeline: Pushing out educational content, student memes, and 
platform highlights consistently. 
● Micro-Collaborations: Partnering with smal campus influencers or specific colege clubs 
for shoutouts. 
● Community Flywheel: Encouraging our early users to invite their friends because the 
product actualy looks good and works wel. 
3. The Tech Stack (The "Work Smart" Tools) 
To build a modern brand without a 20-person team, we need the right stack. Here is what we 
are using to automate the grunt work. 
A. Design & Branding 
● Canva Pro (highly recommended): The bread and butter. We wil use this to house our 
Brand Kit (logos, fonts, colors) and create a l those reusable design templates. 
● Figma (Free+ STUDENT ID): For building the actual Mood Board and colaborating on 
high-fidelity web design tweaks or complex graphics. 
● Pinterest: For gathering inspiration, UI/UX ideas, and aesthetic references for the mood 
board. 
B. Social Media Automation 
Because posting manualy at 6 PM every day is a waste of time. (UNTIL UK HOW HARD IT IS) 
● Metricool or Buffer (Freemium): We wil batch-create content on weekends and use 
these tools to auto-post across Instagram, LinkedIn, and Twitter a l week long. It also gives 
us basic analytics on what’s working. 
C. Community, CRM & Workspace (Cloud/Open Source) 
● Notion (Free for startups/students): Our entire brain. We wil use it for the content 
calendar, storing the brand playbook, meeting notes, and task tracking. 
● Odoo or ERPNext (Open Source): If we need a serious, free/low-cost CRM to track B2B 
leads (like brands or co leges we are pitching), these are powerful open-source ERP 
systems. Note: We wil only set this up when we actualy have too many leads to track in 
Notion. (ODOO IS SHIT NOW BTW )
